newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates unchanged or slightly higher - Freddie Mac.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates unchanged or slightly higher - Freddie Mac.

text.p: U.S. home mortgage rates were unchanged or slightly higher this week as interest rates held steady, Freddie Mac said Thursday.

Thirty-year mortgages stayed at an average of 7.47 percent in the week ended July 18, while 15-year mortgages remained at 7.01 percent. One-year adjustable loans edged higher to 5.55 percent from 5.53 last week.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 8.23 percent, the 15-year 7.76 percent and the adjustable loan 5.97 percent.

"Given the existing economic conditions, we are confident interest rates will stay favourable at least through the summer months," Frank Nothaft, Freddie Mac deputy chief economist, said in a statement.
Fees and points charged by lenders for 30-year and 15-year loans were unchanged at an average of 1.8 percent. Adjustable loan charges also stayed at 1.4 percent this week.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
Separately, the Mortgage Bankers Association of America said the volume of U.S. mortgage refinancing applications jumped 53.3 percent in the week ended July 11.
The total volume of mortgage applications gained 29.6 percent in the latest survey week, while applications to purchase mortgages grew 22.5 percent.
